answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The orchard is the collateral at risk, the velvet the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the grove the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many velvet groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the orchard into smaller, individually useless stakes.
